findings.detail: plan.md declares six files (tests/test_doctor.py, src/swfactory/doctor.py, deploy/islo/bootstrap.sh, deploy/islo/deploy.sh, docs/islo.md, docs/selfhost.md) yet the diff also rewrites `Factory._member_cell` and adds `_own_live_activation` in src/swfactory/backend/service.py — control-plane Cell-ownership logic wholly unrelated to the allow-list, apparently carried in from this branch's earlier `fix:` commits (d9629d5/b24b462). Either the change belongs to a separate PR or plan.md must declare it; a self-hosting PR whose stated scope is doctor+deploy+docs+tests should not silently alter Cell activation/adoption semantics.
findings.title: Diff touches a file plan.md does not list

findings.detail: The `except CellBusy` path that now adopts a live Cell activated by another attempt of the same order adds new behaviour, but the diff contains no test for it; the only coverage in the tree is the threaded four-replica race in tests/test_dispatch_strand.py:380, which reaches this branch only when the interleaving happens to lose an activation. A deterministic test that drives `cell_store.activate` to raise `CellBusy` with a same-owner live Cell (and a foreign-owner one, asserting the 409 survives) should pin both halves of the ownership rule.
findings.title: New CellBusy-adoption branch lands with no test in the diff

findings.detail: plan.md specifies asserting that the `--init minimal` uncertainty wording is gone, but the test asserts `"unsettled" not in text` for all of docs/selfhost.md, so any future unrelated use of an ordinary English word in that evolving document fails a doctor test. Scope the assertion to the retired claim (e.g. `"unsettled whether"` together with `"--init minimal"`), keeping the check coarse as the plan's risk section intended.
findings.title: Doc assertion bans the bare word "unsettled" across the whole file

findings.detail: The test only inspects `allow_hosts_from_shell`'s own signature and source text for the strings `subprocess`/`urllib`/`socket`/`islo `/`curl`, so it passes by construction and would not detect a non-hermetic call in any of the sibling tests it claims to cover (R15). Either drop it as ceremony or make it meaningful — e.g. assert over the source of the whole allow-list test section, or monkeypatch `subprocess.run`/`socket.socket` to raise for the duration of the parity test.
findings.title: test_new_allowlist_tests_are_hermetic asserts almost nothing

findings.detail: deploy/islo/deploy.sh:12-16 now says the `swfactory-orchestrator` profile needs releases.astral.sh and release-assets.githubusercontent.com or its setup script 403s, while this file's header — for the same profile, whose setup_script at line 25 runs that very `astral.sh` installer — still lists only the six old hosts, as does the Orchestrator egress cell in docs/islo.md:9. spec.md open question 2 knowingly left both out of scope, so this is the declared residual, but an operator provisioning from islo.yaml's header will reproduce the 403 this PR exists to prevent; a one-line follow-up should align them.
findings.title: Orchestrator profile is now described with two different allow-lists

findings.detail: `text.find("ALLOW_HOSTS=(")` matches any suffixed name, so an earlier `EXTRA_ALLOW_HOSTS=(...)` or a commented example line in bootstrap.sh would hijack the parity check with a non-empty parse that R13's empty-parse guard cannot catch. Anchoring the search to line start (e.g. scan `splitlines()` for a line beginning with the marker) would make the exact parse rule from spec.md open question 3 enforceable.
findings.title: ALLOW_HOSTS marker is matched as a substring
